fact.thing: RRSP over-contribution cushion before the 1% monthly tax
fact.claim: The CRA lets your unused RRSP contributions go up to $2,000 over your RRSP deduction limit with no penalty. Any amount above that $2,000 is taxed at 1% for each month it stays in the plan. The $2,000 is one cushion that carries across all years, not a new allowance each year and not tied to the March deadline, and you only get it if you were 18 or older at some point in the previous year. The deadline on the CRA page right now is March 2, 2026, for the 2025 tax year; the CRA has not yet posted the deadline for the 2026 tax year (not confirmed).

felt.how: 1% a month on the $3,000 past the $2,000 cushion, 12 months, on the post's $5,000-over example

sources.label: CRA – Excess Contributions
sources.what: Generally, you have to pay a tax of 1% per month on your unused contributions that exceed your RRSP deduction limit by more than $2,000.

sources.what: Also, you can only qualify for the additional $2,000 amount if you were 18 or older at any time in 2024.

plain.what: An RRSP is a retirement account where you park money and pay less tax now. The CRA lets you go up to $2,000 over your RRSP deduction limit — the most you're allowed to put in — with no penalty. Anything over that $2,000 gets taxed 1% for every month it sits there.
plain.so_what: If you're $5,000 over, the extra $3,000 past the cushion costs you $30 a month, so $360 is gone after a year.
plain.do: Open your latest notice of assessment and write down your RRSP deduction limit and what you've put in so far.
